utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. This is case IT-99-37-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Slobodan Milosevic, Milan Milutinovic, Nikola Sainovic, Dragoljub Ojdanic, Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution is represented by myself, Prosecutor Carla Del Ponte, with trial attorney Milbert Shin and case manager Rebecca Graham. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Prosecutor. Well, for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Toma Fila, an attorney from Belgrade, and together with Mr. Zoran Jovanovic, also a lawyer from Belgrade, I represent the Defence of Mr. Nikola Sainovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila. Mr. Sainovic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can follow it in the language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then may I have your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Nikola Sainovic, born on 7 December 1948.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit again. Before we go on, I have to say sorry, to all of the people here and those assisting us behind doors, to have a hearing at this late hour of the day; however, this was the only available time we could find, due to the heavy schedule of trials which are going on at this moment. This is an Initial Appearance to be conducted in accordance with Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of this Tribunal. The purpose of this hearing is, firstly, for the Court to be satisfied that the accused understands the indictment; and secondly, for the accused to enter a plea to the indictment. In regard to the first question, Mr. Fila, may I take it that your client has received a copy of the indictment in a language that he can understand and that you have had the opportunity of going through the indictment with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Does your client wish to have the indictment read out in full in the courtroom or is he prepared to waive that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My client is ready to waive the right of the reading of the indictment. He is well acquainted with it and there is no need for the reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we'll have the entry of the plea of the accused. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days of the Initial Appearance, but he may enter a plea today if he so wishes. Mr. Fila, what is your client's intention? Does he wish to enter a plea today or do it later?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my client will plead today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sainovic, will you please stand again. Have you heard what your counsel has said? Has the indictment been explained to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have studied the indictment carefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Now I will read to you the counts in the Second Amended Indictment. You will then enter a plea to each count. Please confine your answers to either "guilty" or "not guilty." Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 1 of the indictment charges you with deportation, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(d) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 2 charges you with other inhumane acts, i.e., forcible transfer, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(i) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead to that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And counts 3 and 4 relate to the alleged killing of the Kosovo Albanian civilians between the 1st of January and the 20th of June in 1999. Count 3 charges you with murder, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(a) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And count 4 charges you with murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute the Tribunal, and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And finally, count 5 charges you with persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute. How do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This completes the pleas. Now you may sit again. There are a couple of miscellaneous matters I have to deal with at this moment. First I would like to remind Madam Prosecutor of her duty under Rule 66(A)(i) to make available to the Defence, in the language that the accused understands and within 30 days from now, all the supporting materials that accompanied the indictment and all prior statements obtained from the accused. Of course I take it that that obligation will be discharged, but do you have any comments on that, madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just to inform, we will be disclosing the material both in English and B/C/S, the language of the accused. The total quantity of the material in English and B/C/S will be 14 binders in total. For all but one of the binders we have all material ready in English and B/C/S, but in relation to this binder, there are 48 pages still in the process of translation in B/C/S. We will endeavour to have the translations completed on this binder, all ready for disclosure by Friday, 17 May. However, before we disclose the materials, we will be filing a motion for non-disclosure of the material to the public. We will also be filing a motion to extend the protective measures applied to the Milosevic case to certain witnesses to this case and will await a response to that motion before we can disclose such materials. In the Milosevic case, we sought and obtained permission from the Chamber to use pseudonyms and not to disclose the statements of certain witnesses until 30 days before they testify, for the amici, and 10 days before for the accused. So presuming we are ready to start disclosure as soon as possible, by Monday, 6 May, with regard to material not the subject of the motion to extend protective measures because we await the decision. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, madam. We will wait for the motion from you. And the second question will be the next hearing, a Status Conference. I note that the Status Conference for the co-accused, Mr. Ojdanic, has been scheduled to take place on Friday, the 21st of June, at 3 p.m. We'll have a joint hearing for the purpose of the Status Conference. This concludes today's hearing. And are there -- I wonder if there's anything the parties wish to raise at this moment. For the Prosecution? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DEL PONTE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, just one thing. I have carefully listened to what Madam Prosecutor had to say. In the Milosevic case there are amici curiae. Here there are none, so this ten days deadline is not acceptable to me. Thirty days, however, would be acceptable. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will consider it in due course. Thank you. Then there being no other things to be dealt with, this hearing is adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Initial Appearance adjourned at
